title: Hong Kong privacy commissioner says initial information shows Gleneagles Hong Kong Hospital app was hacked; Department of Health follows up
date_note: The Department of Health press release (24 Nov) is the first public statement; it says the hospital found the unauthorized activity on 18 November and notified the Department on 23 November.
geo_basis: Hospital in Hong Kong named by the Department of Health; city-level pin
summary: Hong Kong's Department of Health says Gleneagles Hong Kong Hospital found unauthorized activity affecting its patient mobile app on 18 November, with unauthorized access to some patients' personal data. The privacy commissioner's office, per RTHK, says initial information indicates a hacker attack, and has opened an investigation. The Department requires the hospital to notify affected patients. Neither source gives a number of patients.
plain: A Hong Kong private hospital's patient app was accessed without authorization, exposing some patients' personal data. The privacy office says initial information points to a hacker attack.
exec: The Department of Health will check whether the hospital breached the Private Healthcare Facilities Ordinance and will take regulatory action if needed.
action: The Department of Health advises that the hospital must notify all affected patients as soon as possible, and it reminds licensed private healthcare facilities to strengthen information security.

sources.name: Hong Kong Department of Health (government press release)

validation.note: Department of Health press release (primary) plus RTHK reporting the PCPD statement; RTHK adds the PCPD's hacker-attack assessment.

review.note: Compared dates 18/23/24 Nov, unauthorized access, no patient number, hospital duties against DoH release; hacker-attack assessment against RTHK PCPD report
